title: Customers should get a receipt when their invoice is paid + Finance needs a list of overdue invoices + Expired coupons are still accepted at checkout
prompt:
Three related tickets in invoices, payments and coupons are being delivered together as one change. Implement all of them in this working tree.

### Ticket 1: Customers should get a receipt when their invoice is paid

Customers have no confirmation that we received their payment. When an invoice is marked as paid, email the customer a receipt: the subject is "Payment received for order <order number>" and the body is "We have received your payment for order <order number>. Thank you!".

It is an ordinary notification, so it also appears in the customer's notification list, with the kind `payment_received`.

### Ticket 2: Finance needs a list of overdue invoices

Finance chases late payers by hand. Add `GET /invoices/overdue` (admin only) returning every invoice that is still `open` and whose due date has passed, the one that fell due longest ago first. Each entry is the invoice plus a `daysOverdue` field: the whole days since the due date, and at least 1 for anything that is overdue. Paid and void invoices never appear.

### Ticket 3: Expired coupons are still accepted at checkout

Coupons carry an optional expiry timestamp (`expiresAt`), but checkout never looks at it: a customer applied a coupon that expired weeks ago and still got the discount.

Reject a coupon with a 400 and the message "coupon has expired" once the current time has reached its expiry time. Coupons without an expiry, and coupons that expire in the future, keep working.

couplings.note: t040 x t001: Both add a coupon check immediately after the unknown-coupon check in issueInvoice (billing/service.ts).
